title: Correct voltage calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly computes the accelerating voltage using energy conservation, obtaining approximately 3.34×10⁵ V.

title: Correct electric field strength
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the uniform electric field strength from voltage and distance, obtaining approximately 8.35×10⁴ V/m.

title: Energy conservation application
description: Important: Student applies the work-energy theorem or conservation of energy, equating kinetic energy gain to electrical potential energy loss.

title: Uniform field relationship
description: Important: Student correctly uses the relationship U = Ed for a uniform electric field to connect voltage, field strength, and distance.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student maintains consistent SI units throughout calculations and includes correct units in final answers.

title: Sign error in energy relation
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses sign in energy relation (e.g., qU = -½mv² instead of qU = ½mv² for proton acceleration).

title: Incorrect field formula
description: Pitfall: Student uses incorrect formula for electric field (e.g., E = V/d² or E = Vd instead of E = V/d).
